(1) the psychosis-prone (specifically schizotypal and general psychotic) personality traits are associated with the dopaminergic system; and (2) these personality traits are associated in a unique and robust manner with activity in regions that are implicated in DA transmission and that are implicated in procedural learning, including the basal ganglia and thalamus.
the EPQ-R P scale correlates with activity in the basal ganglion and thalamus during procedural learning.

the personality dimension of psychoticism (EPQ-R Psychotic scale) is associated with increased activation of the striatum, thalamus and insula during a procedural learning task, and is associated with increased psychoticism (STA Schizotypal scale) during the same task.

the EPQ-R P scale, which was originally developed to assess the propensity to develop schizophrenia and other psychoses, may also be useful for identifying individuals who are vulnerable to the effects of drugs that block DA D2 receptors.
